$comment: On-device money-request detection (security.md rule 9). Friction, not protection: attackers can read these rules. Regexes use a portable ASCII subset: [0-9] not \\d, explicit (?<![0-9A-Za-z]) / (?![0-9A-Za-z]) instead of \\b, because ICU (Swift) and Java treat \\d and \\b as Unicode-aware while JS does not. Phrases are compared after normalisation. Starter list: review before launch. Warning kind: the first kind in warningKindPriority whose rule applies. pixKey applies only when the normalised message also contains a pixKeyContextWords entry (a phone number or e-mail alone is normal chat). newNumber applies when a matched urgency phrase is in newNumberPhrases (the falso parente opener), or when the normalised message contains a newAccountPhrases entry and also a registries/family-terms.json term as a whole word or a matched urgency phrase. On Bipe nobody sees phone numbers (ADR 0015), so the opener says new account instead of new number. Whole word: replace each run of characters outside [0-9a-z] in the normalised message with one space, then look for the term with a space on each side. newAccountPhrases need the context because "conta nova" alone is normal chat (a bank account, a new account on another app). Link hosts: linkPatterns matches (every match) on the host-folded message, which is normalize(message) with registries/homoglyphs.json except its ASCII keys outside [0-9a-z] (@, $ and | cannot be part of a host name). Each folded host has a plain host: the same UTF-16 range in normalize(message) without folding. deliveryFee (the fake-delivery fee scam: parcel held, pay a fee by link) applies when there is a link host and the normalised message also contains an entry from each of deliveryParcelWords, deliveryHoldWords and deliveryFeeWords. linkPatterns finds bare domains with a fixed TLD list, lowercase only. Link hosts get uppercase links because normalize() lowercases first. A case-insensitive flag is not an option: case-insensitive matching differs between ICU, Java and V8 for characters like U+017F. lookalikeLink (a link that copies a bank, government or company address) applies when a folded host, without its dots and hyphens, contains a lookalikeBrandTokens entry, or when one of its labels (the parts between dots and hyphens) is a lookalikeHostLabels entry, and the plain host is not an officialDomains entry or a subdomain of one. The plain host catches homoglyph spellings: "іtau.com.br" with a Cyrillic і and "bradesc0.com.br" fold to an official name but are not one. Tokens are not the reserved names: short names like inter, neon, pix and sus are inside common words and hosts. bankAlert (a fake bank alert: your account or Pix is blocked, fix it at this link) applies when there is a link host and the normalised message also contains an entry from bankAlertSubjectWords and from bankAlertThreatWords. lookalikeHostLabels are short public-body and bank names (bcb, gov, inss, receita, detran, bb) that are too short to match inside a host: "valoresareceber-bcb.site" warns, "receitas.globo.com" does not. Whole-word lists (remoteAppInstallWords, remoteAppNames, pinRequestSecretWords, pinRequestSupportWords) match like family terms: each run of characters outside [0-9a-z] in the normalised message becomes one space, then the term must have a space on each side. extortion (a threat with a payment demand: sextortion, "I know where you live") applies when the normalised message contains an extortionThreatPhrases entry and an extortionDemandWords entry. A threat without a payment demand is not this kind. remoteApp (a request to install a remote-access app) applies when the message has a remoteAppInstallWords entry and either a remoteAppNames entry, or a link host whose plain host is not an officialDomains or appStoreDomains entry or a subdomain of one together with a remoteAppBankWords entry. pinRequest (fake Bipe support asks for the PIN or a code) applies when the normalised message contains a pinRequestAskPhrases entry, a pinRequestSecretWords entry and a pinRequestSupportWords entry.
